rationale: bugs_open/343 (029's still-open half): the outstanding-awaited set has two representations nothing reconciles - the awaited_requests table (drives the response consumer) and the AwaitedRequests JSONB map (drives the advance decision). Verified at source: persistAwaitingStateWithRetry's beat-the-park check keys on STEP NAME via a bare "response" literal, not the request id, and returns nil WITHOUT persisting - so every re-registration of an already-answered step name (each iteration N+1 of a loop's call_handler) reads as an arrival, the caller reads nil as success, and it then inserts an orphan table row and arms a timeout for a request no map holds. The orchestration sits in EXECUTING_STEP with no waiting awaited request until the 4-hour reaper. Newly verified this round: two of the four response branches write no arrival marker at all, and one of them (output_mapping) is live on real call_agent await paths. This round: record which request a reply answered in all four branches; key the check on that id; type the park outcome so a non-persisting park is unrepresentable; surface map-vs-table divergence at the decision it corrupts, with enforcement opt-in and default OFF. The wedge's FIRST-death mechanism is not explained by this change and nothing here asserts it.

plan.summary: bugs_open/343: the park's beat-the-park check keys on STEP NAME, not the request id, and returns nil WITHOUT persisting on a hit - so every re-registration of an already-answered step name reads as an arrival, the caller reads nil as success and inserts an orphan awaited_requests row plus a timeout for a request no state map holds. The orchestration then sits in EXECUTING_STEP with no waiting awaited request until the 4-hour reaper. This change records WHICH request each reply answered (in all four response branches - two wrote no marker at all, and one of those, output_mapping, is live on real call_agent paths), keys the check on that id so stale residue parks normally, makes a non-persisting park unrepresentable via a typed park outcome, and cross-checks the map-derived advance decision against the awaited_requests table with detection unconditional and enforcement opt-in default OFF.

edits.rationale: Record WHICH awaited request a recorded reply answered, so the arrival check can ask about identity rather than presence. Written in ALL FOUR branches of applyResponseToState: two of them (output_mapping :2796-2821, default :2902) wrote no arrival marker of any kind, and output_mapping is live on real call_agent await paths (sql_for_agents/107_image_build_handler.sql:589 call_variant_gen, :1119 call_imagery_gen) - so a reply beating the park there is invisible to the check today. Also converges the two bare "response" literals (:2860, :2876) onto awaitedResponseMarker, whose doc comment already claims to govern the check but did not.

THE DEFECT. Key the arrival check on the recorded id: same id = a reply to THIS request genuinely beat the park (skip, consumer owns the continuation); DIFFERENT id = stale residue of an earlier request under the same step name, so PARK NORMALLY - this single discrimination is what closes the wedge; no id = dated legacy branch preserving today's behaviour for the mixed-fleet window after the roll. The genuine race exists only where the row is pre-registered before the send, which is five callers, not one: spawn_actions.go:115, dispatch_actions.go:229 and three thunder_prepare_*_dispatch.go actions.

Make 'returned success without persisting' unrepresentable at the type level. persistAwaitingStateWithRetry returns (parkOutcome, error) and the sole caller processAwaitResponse must switch: on parkSkippedReplyArrived it performs NO InsertAwaitedRequest and arms NO timeout goroutine, and drops the in-memory entry so this state cannot re-assert it. That kills the orphan-row producer outright. Reverting the signature fails compilation, which is the point - the compiler now forces every caller to say which case it is in. Returns true either way, preserving today's external behaviour at the call site: the executor must stop driving the step, and the consumer's already-advanced state is authoritative.

withoutResponseMarker must strip BOTH markers on the carry path. Post-change the id is the MORE dangerous of the two to carry: an id equal to the request being parked forges exactly the identity the check now keys on, whereas a bare marker alone now only reaches the legacy branch. The presence pre-check must look for either key, not only the first - an id-only container would otherwise be returned unchanged.

The table's answer to 'what is outstanding', which the advance decision has never had. Returns ROWS rather than a count because detection needs only len()>0 but enforcement needs the rows to re-adopt, and one method means a count and a fetch cannot drift apart. excludeRequestID is the request being completed: it legitimately sits in 'processing' under the consumer's own claim at that instant, since the row is marked complete only after the state save succeeds. Reuses the existing awaitedRequestColumns and scanAwaitedRequestRow rather than adding a second scan shape.

+		WHERE orchestration_id = $1 AND request_id <> $2
+		  AND status IN ('waiting', 'processing', 'retrying')`
+	...rows.Next() loop over scanAwaitedRequestRow...

edits.rationale: Cross-check the map-derived allDone against the table at the one moment their disagreement becomes a wrong decision. Detection is UNCONDITIONAL - logged and written to agent_error_log (error_code=await_divergence) whatever the flag says - because today the decision reads the map alone and a divergence is recorded nowhere. Enforcement (adopt the rows, re-park, do not advance) is gated on the new opt-in key so that with it OFF the decision is byte-identical to today. A query error warns and proceeds as today: a cross-check must never become a new way to fail. TWO HAZARDS, both real, both reasons the default is off: (a) adopting a row means waiting out its timeout, after which the retry driver replays the request and real side effects re-run; (b) the table must stay a cross-check, never a naive replacement for the map's optimistic-lock CAS, which is what serialises two pods racing to advance. Known benign detection window: a sibling request is 'processing' until marked complete after its own save - if noise appears the query needs a grace age on young 'processing' rows, not deletion.

New authority on a shared seam (the park/response protocol every await_response step crosses) ships as an opt-in FIELD with the unsafe side OFF, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2 - not as a documented rule, because a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share. Plan-level, so it does NOT enter the WFA-013 optional-key budget; if a later change moves it onto an action's config it does, and the cron parity test applies. Under the RFC_022 narrowing this is council-gate scope, not architecture-scope: opt-in yes, unsafe default OFF yes, zero live consumers yes - and that third condition is TAUTOLOGICAL for a newly-named field, stated here as such rather than offered as a measurement.

edits.rationale: Mutation-provable cover, three new files plus the register and LANDMINES entries that ship in the same commit. The decisive test is TestParkProceedsOnStaleMarkerFromAnEarlierRequest: restore presence-keying and it fails with the park skipping and issuing no UPDATE - the wedge, reproduced in CI. TestParkSkipsWhenThisRequestHasAlreadyBeenAnswered asserts NO UPDATE and NO INSERT on the skip path, which is the orphan-row producer's tombstone. Detector and enforcer are mutated SEPARATELY (a mutation that passes may have hit a guard in series): removing enforcement kills only the enforce test while the detection tests still pass. Also: TestIDMarkerIsWrittenInEveryResponseBranch table-drives all four branches so deleting any single write fails exactly that subtest, and TestCarryStripsBothResponseMarkers pins the id-only case. Register RSH-012 + WFA-021 and the LANDMINES entry for the legacy branch land in this same commit per the platform-seams ordering exemption's condition (2).

grounded_in: bugs_open/343: 'That give-up is where the defect is: instead of failing the orchestration, the parent stops writing state altogether. It sits in EXECUTING_STEP holding no waiting awaited request, so nothing routine notices it - only the 4-hour stale reaper.'

bugs_open/343 measured entry condition, with its positive control: '31 call_handlers reached retry_version=3, status=error in the retained window; 0 ever registered another call_handler. Positive control that could have come out otherwise, and did: 1,387 healthy call_handlers, 1,054 (76%) continued.'
bugs_open/343 on the two modes: '20 WEDGED - iteration N+1's spawn_handler IS registered, its call_handler never is (this bug). 11 STOPPED - no N+1 spawn_handler either.'

coordinator.go persistAwaitingStateWithRetry, the pre-fix check: 'if existingData, exists := freshState.CollectedData[state.AwaitedRequests[reqID].StepName].(map[string]interface{}); exists { if _, hasResponse := existingData["response"]; hasResponse { ... return nil } }' - keyed on StepName, returns nil BEFORE repo.UpdateState and before InsertAwaitedRequest.

coordinator.go applyResponseToState output_mapping branch: 'state.CollectedData[stepName] = mappedResult' with only response_received_at and response_status added - no arrival marker at all, and this branch is live: sql_for_agents/107_image_build_handler.sql:589 (call_variant_gen, "action": "call_agent") and :1119 (call_imagery_gen) both carry output_mapping.

coordinator.go handleCompleteResponse: 'allDone := len(freshState.AwaitedRequests) == 0' - decided from the JSONB map alone; the awaited_requests table is consulted nowhere before the advance, and MarkAwaitedRequestComplete runs only after UpdateState succeeds.

The five pre-registering callers, enumerated rather than asserted: preRegisterAwaitedRequest (spawn_actions.go:162) is called from spawn_actions.go:115, dispatch_actions.go:229, thunder_prepare_resume_url_dispatch.go:141, thunder_prepare_object_url_dispatch.go:205, thunder_prepare_object_urls_dispatch.go:171 - the row is inserted BEFORE the send on all five, so the beat-the-park race is not spawn-shaped.

Only two INSERT INTO awaited_requests sites exist (state.go InsertAwaitedRequest, spawn_actions.go preRegisterAwaitedRequest) and neither is on a retry path: handleRecoverableError replays via payload.ReplayRequest and UpdateAwaitedRequestRetry only UPDATEs. So a retry can never mint a second rv0 row, and the second row in a wedged pair came from a fresh execution.

Owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1: an addition to a shared vocabulary needs an RFC only when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. Restoring 'a park persists the awaited entry' is repairing the stated guarantee, not altering it.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2: 'when a seam's widest branch is licensed by "callers must all be X", make X a field with the unsafe default OFF ... A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.' Hence await_reconcile_enforce rather than a documented rule.

RFC_022 narrowing (owner ruling 2026-08-11): opt-in, unsafe side default OFF, zero live consumers named - all three hold, and the third is tautological for a newly-named field, stated as such rather than dressed as a measurement.

bugs_open/343 on what this does NOT do: 'Nothing in awaited_requests separates the 20 from the 11 ... This route is closed' and the first death - why the child stopped answering and the parent never registered iteration N+1's call_handler - remains unexplained by any edit here.
plan.risks: (1) THE LEGACY BRANCH is the sharpest thing to check: a marker with no id is treated as ARRIVED, which is today's behaviour and is deliberate for the mixed-fleet window - parking instead would double-drive an old pod's real reply. It is dated in the source and has a LANDMINES entry, because it looks exactly like the presence-keyed logic the rest of the diff condemns. (2) ENFORCEMENT, if anyone ever switches it on: adopting a table row means waiting out its timeout, after which the retry driver replays the request and REAL SIDE EFFECTS RE-RUN; and the table must stay a cross-check, never a naive replacement for the map's optimistic-lock CAS, which is what serialises two pods racing to advance. Default is false and no workflow sets it. (3) DETECTION NOISE: a sibling request legitimately sits in 'processing' until it is marked complete AFTER its own state save, so a ms-scale false-positive window exists by construction; the remedy if it appears is a grace age on young 'processing' rows, not deleting the check. No baseline exists - the obvious 'divergence census reads 0' is VACUOUS on this estate today because there are zero orchestrations in AWAITING_RESPONSES and zero non-terminal awaited rows, so 0/0 is arithmetically forced. (4) The skip path now returns true having persisted nothing; the caller's only consumer logs on needsWaiting, so external behaviour is unchanged, but a reviewer should confirm that reading. (5) WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not explain the FIRST death - why a child stopped answering and the parent never registered iteration N+1's call_handler. 343 stays OPEN and nothing in the diff or its comments says otherwise.
